entradas.text: In fact, we were busier than ever now that Monica's work with the Commission on the Status of Women was in full swing.

She spent most days of the week meeting with Ciara or members of the Assembly, discussing how to implement the new laws I had passed. I often had to pitch in with chores or help Deana with her homework myself.
A reversal of the usual husband-and-wife roles, to be sure. Lileas Graf would be furious if she knew.
I was dozing on the couch after yet another frozen TV dinner when I heard the key turn in the lock. Monica stumbled into the hall.
"Honey, I'm home!"
It was late at night when I exited Serge's car, walked through the gates of the presidential complex and unlocked my front door.
Monica and I weren't speaking much at all these days. I'd been spending more and more time in the office, just to avoid the chilly atmosphere that awaited me at home.
The lights in the kitchen were still on. I walked in to find Monica sitting alone at the table, pouring the dregs of a bottle of Kebij into her glass.
"Well, if it isn't the savior of Sordish women! Our knight in shining armor!"
"You're drunk."
entradas.menu: "You're drunk."

entradas.text: "Don't start with me. I'm not in the mood."
entradas.menu: "Don't start with me. I'm not in the mood."

entradas.text: "At your service, ma'am."
entradas.menu: "At your service, ma'am."

entradas.text: "I was being sarcastic, Anton."
"Very perceptive, Mr. President."
"I think I know what this is about."
entradas.menu: "I think I know what this is about."

entradas.text: "*You're* not in the mood?"
"Ciara called and told me what happened with her women's rights bill. Because she knew I'd want to know."

"Ciara's been filling me in on her commission's progress. Apparently Lotherberg Group lobbyists have convinced some Assembly members to pushback against the equal pay section of the women's rights decree."
"This would never have happened if you'd allowed me to get involved."
"That's not true."
entradas.menu: "That's not true."

entradas.text: "Ciara's been doing her best."
entradas.menu: "Ciara's been doing her best."

entradas.text: "Ciara's too radical and you know it. Those old men needed a skirt-wearing housewife like me to convince them women's rights aren't just for spinsters and lesbians."
Monica hiccuped.
"This was my big chance. The one thing I'd wanted to do since before I even met you. And you -- Anton Rayne -- you ruined it!"
"Great news, isn't it? We won!"
entradas.menu: "Great news, isn't it? We won!"

entradas.text: "So... you're drinking to celebrate?"
entradas.menu: "So... you're drinking to celebrate?"

entradas.text: "*You* won. While forcing your own wife to the sidelines. Congratulations."
"Yes, I'm celebrating being a mere footnote in your great victory."
"I've advanced the status of women further than any president in Sordish history. Be grateful."
entradas.menu: "I've advanced the status of women further than any president in Sordish history. Be grateful."

entradas.text: "I did this for you, Monica. I thought you'd be happy."
entradas.menu: "I did this for you, Monica. I thought you'd be happy."

entradas.text: "All I wanted to do was protect you. You've seen what this job has done to me these past three years."
entradas.menu: "All I wanted to do was protect you. You've seen what this job has done to me these past three years."

entradas.text: "You're a First Lady, not a politician. You knew that going in."
entradas.menu: "You're a First Lady, not a politician. You knew that going in."

entradas.text: "Other women would kill to be married to the President of Sordland. Can't you just shut up and be satisfied?"
entradas.menu: "Other women would kill to be married to the President of Sordland. Can't you just shut up and be satisfied?"

entradas.text: "Oh."
entradas.menu: "Oh."

entradas.text: "Let me explain."
entradas.menu: "Let me explain."

entradas.text: "Vetoed, Anton? It's not enough to deny your wife opportunities -- you've got to screw over every women in Sordland?"
"Oh, have I ever."
"Then you don't know me."
Monica sighed deeply.
"I am grateful. But I can't be happy about it."
"You really don't know me, do you?"
"I thought we'd be a team. How stupid of me."
"I don't think I can do this anymore. I'm calling Evelyn's divorce attorney."
"Wait. Please. Let's talk about this."
entradas.menu: "Wait. Please. Let's talk about this."

entradas.text: "You can't divorce me! At least not until next year."
entradas.menu: "You can't divorce me! At least not until next year."

entradas.text: "You wouldn't dare."
entradas.menu: "You wouldn't dare."

entradas.text: "What is there to talk about? It's been over since that day you hit me on the balcony."
"That's what you care about? Your chances of getting re-elected?"
"This is one thing you can't forbid me from doing."
"What are you going to do? Hit me again?"
I reached into my briefcase and pulled out the photo of us I had taken from my old office.
entradas.menu: Show Monica the framed photo you took from your old office.

entradas.text: "Look how happy we are here. We loved each other once. We can still fix this."
entradas.menu: "Look how happy we are here. We loved each other once. We can still fix this."

entradas.text: "Look how determined we are here. If you divorce me now, we risk losing everything we fought so hard for."
entradas.menu: "Look how determined we are here. If you divorce me now, we risk losing everything we fought so hard for."

entradas.text: "It's too late for talking."
"I-- I don't know, Anton."
Monica looked at it. Tears began to form in her eyes.
"If you leave me now, my public opinion might not survive the blow. I could lose the election, Monica."
entradas.menu: "If you leave me now, my public opinion might not survive the blow. I could lose the election, Monica."

entradas.text: "I'll pay you to stay. At least until after the election."
entradas.menu: "I'll pay you to stay. At least until after the election."

entradas.text: "Bribery? You're going to treat me like one of your crooked politician pals?"
"Hey, you're the one who said you wanted to be involved in politics."
entradas.menu: "Hey, you're the one who said you wanted to be involved in politics."

entradas.text: "Think about the kids. You'll be able to provide for them without having to ask me for a cent."
entradas.menu: "Think about the kids. You'll be able to provide for them without having to ask me for a cent."

entradas.text: "The people of Sordland love you more than me, after all."
entradas.menu: "The people of Sordland love you more than me, after all."

entradas.text: "And then whatever progress Sordland has made for women's rights will be lost as well."
entradas.menu: "And then whatever progress Sordland has made for women's rights will be lost as well."

entradas.text: "And then whatever progress I've managed to make for this country will be lost as well."
entradas.menu: "And then whatever progress I've managed to make for this country will be lost as well."

entradas.text: Monica cradled her head in her hands.
"We will remain married in name alone. You'll sleep in the guesthouse and interact with Deana and myself only when necessary. The day after the election, I'm filing for divorce."
"You can't control whether I see Deana! She's my daughter, too."
entradas.menu: "You can't control whether I see Deana! She's my daughter, too."

entradas.text: "I can accept those conditions."
entradas.menu: "I can accept those conditions."

entradas.text: "All right. I'll hold off on talking to the lawyer. At least until after you're re-elected."
"Thank you, Monica."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Monica."

entradas.text: "That gives me more time to figure out how I can win you back."
entradas.menu: "That gives me more time to figure out how I can win you back."

entradas.text: Monica gave me the faintest of nods.
"I couldn't care less about your public opinion."
"I couldn't care less about your so-called progress. You failed on the issue that matters most to me."
Monica cradled her head in her hands.
"I'm calling the lawyer tomorrow. We can wait a few weeks to tell Deana."
"I will not let you insult me like this."
She pushed her chair roughly away.
Monica's expression softened slightly.
"I won't need to ask for a cent because I'm taking everything. You hear me, Anton? Everything."
Monica clenched her jaw.
"If you think you're going to keep custody of her, you're goddamn mistaken."
entradas.menu: "If you think you're going to keep custody of her, you're goddamn mistaken."

entradas.text: "I'm going to make sure you wind up with nothing."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to make sure you wind up with nothing."

entradas.text: "But I do care about the progress you've made towards women's equality. Even if you've blocked me from taking part in it."
"Monica. Look at this photograph."
entradas.menu: "Monica. Look at this photograph."

entradas.text: "Then maybe you care about money?"
entradas.menu: "Then maybe you care about money?"

entradas.text: I reached into my briefcase and pulled out the photo of us I had taken from my old office.
"Fine. I'll respect your wishes."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I'll respect your wishes."

entradas.text: Monica glared at me.
"I don't want her around you. Not the way you are now."
Monica looked at me for a long moment.
"I wish it hadn't come to this, Anton."
Monica's expression hardened.
"I'm sorry, Anton. It's too late."
"I'd rather be penniless than spend another moment married to you."
I picked up her empty glass and threw it to the ground. Shards flew everywhere.
entradas.menu: Pick up her glass and smash it on the ground.

entradas.text: "Screw you."
entradas.menu: "Screw you."

entradas.text: "I'm sorry. I've been a horrible husband and father."
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry. I've been a horrible husband and father."

entradas.text: "See you in court."
entradas.menu: "See you in court."

entradas.text: "Me, neither."
entradas.menu: "Me, neither."

entradas.text: Right away, I heard the sound of footsteps running towards the kitchen. Deana burst in and threw herself between me and Monica.
"Papa, don't hurt her! Please!"
"Deana. Pack a bag. We're staying at a hotel tonight."
With one last furious look at me, Monica ushered Deana upstairs. I'd lost both of them. Possibly forever.
I sighed, grabbed a broom and started sweeping up the broken glass on the floor.
Monica's lips formed a thin line.
"I'm taking Deana to a hotel tonight. I don't want to see you when I get back."
With one last furious look at me, Monica marched upstairs to get Deana.
"I-- I'm taking Deana to a hotel tonight. I think it's for the best that we don't see each other for a while."
After they left, I rang up Orso Hawker. I may have lost my wife, but I was going to keep my daughter.
entradas.menu: Call Orso Hawker to ensure you keep custody of Deana.

entradas.text: After they left, I sat there in the kitchen for a long time, replaying my 20-year marriage over and over in my head.
entradas.menu: Do nothing.

entradas.text: After they left, I sat there in the kitchen for a long time, replaying my 20-year marriage over and over in my head.
With one last regretful look at me, Monica trudged upstairs to get Deana.
"Can-- can you find somewhere else to sleep tonight? I need to be alone for a little while."
I nodded numbly. A short time later, bag in hand, I called Serge and asked him to take me to the closest hotel.
As we were driving away, I took a look back at the house where my wife and daughter were sleeping. I hoped I hadn't lost them forever.
"Where were you?"
entradas.menu: "Where were you?"

entradas.text: I kissed her. Her breath smelled like gin.
entradas.menu: Kiss her.

entradas.text: "Don't you know how late it is?"
entradas.menu: "Don't you know how late it is?"

entradas.text: "I was just having a few drinks with Ciara."
After weeks of late nights, Monica, Ciara and the women's rights commission had succeeded in getting their bill through the Assembly.
It was as comprehensive as they could have hoped for. I was looking forward to celebrating with my wife.
But it had been hours since I'd gotten home, and she still wasn't there.
After weeks of late nights, Monica, Ciara and the women's rights commission had succeeded in getting their bill through the Assembly.
The result wasn't as comprehensive as they'd hoped for, but it was a good start. I was looking forward to celebrating with my wife.
After weeks of late nights, Monica, Ciara and the women's rights commission had succeeded in presenting their bill before the Assembly -- only for it to fail.
I left work early, expecting my wife would be in need of comfort.
After weeks of late nights, Monica, Ciara and the women's rights commission had succeeded in getting their bill through the Assembly -- only for me to veto it.
I left work early in order to explain myself to my wife.
"The Lotherberg lobbyists are already trying to negotiate over our equal pay law. But we showed those pricks who's boss!"
She hiccuped.
"I can't believe we did it! Anton, this is such amazing news."
"I'm actually amazed any version of our bill passed, given how stacked the Assembly was against us. But of course she wants to keep pushing for more."
"We were so close to winning, Anton. Those goddamn Assembly pricks ruined it all."
"You could've invited me to the celebrations."
entradas.menu: "You could've invited me to the celebrations."

entradas.text: She collapsed onto the couch and buried her head in her hands.
"So you decided to get juiced."
entradas.menu: "So you decided to get juiced."

entradas.text: "You could've invited me to the commiseration session."
entradas.menu: "You could've invited me to the commiseration session."

entradas.text: "We had to get drunk after what you did to our bill. Vetoed, Anton? What on Earth were you thinking?"
She collapsed onto the couch and buried her head in her hands.
"This was my big chance. The one thing I'd wanted to do since before I even met you. And you -- Anton Rayne -- you ruined it!"
"I didn't think this bill was good enough. We'll have another chance next year."
entradas.menu: "I didn't think this bill was good enough. We'll have another chance next year."

entradas.text: "Sorry, I changed my mind. It would be too unpopular of a decision."
entradas.menu: "Sorry, I changed my mind. It would be too unpopular of a decision."

entradas.text: "Sorry, I changed my mind. You ladies were asking for too much, too quickly."
entradas.menu: "Sorry, I changed my mind. You ladies were asking for too much, too quickly."

entradas.text: "Well, yes. Isn't it what a man would do?"
"Oh, you would've found it boring. And somebody had to look after Deana."
"My God. I'm starting to see what I put you through for all those years."
entradas.menu: "My God. I'm starting to see what I put you through for all those years."

entradas.text: "I believe you're turning into a politician, Mrs. Rayne."
entradas.menu: "I believe you're turning into a politician, Mrs. Rayne."

entradas.text: "I'm not sure I like this side of you."
entradas.menu: "I'm not sure I like this side of you."

entradas.text: "Get used to it, baby."
"Seriously, Anton -- this is what I want to do. I've never felt so alive."
"I'm happy if you're happy."
entradas.menu: "I'm happy if you're happy."

entradas.text: I pulled her into a hug, and she wrapped her arms around me tightly.
entradas.menu: Hug her.

entradas.text: "I'm glad something good came out of these hellish years."
entradas.menu: "I'm glad something good came out of these hellish years."

entradas.text: I opened my briefcase and pulled out the photograph I'd taken from my old office on that fateful night with Petr.
entradas.menu: Show her the framed photo you took from your old office.

entradas.text: "Oh, wow. Look at us."
"Don't you worry. The best is yet to come."
"Who would have thought we would wind up as Sordland's most powerful couple?"
entradas.menu: "Who would have thought we would wind up as Sordland's most powerful couple?"

entradas.text: "We were so young. We had no idea what was in store."
entradas.menu: "We were so young. We had no idea what was in store."

entradas.text: "I'm still as madly in love with you as I was the day that photo was taken."
entradas.menu: "I'm still as madly in love with you as I was the day that photo was taken."

entradas.text: "Now all we have to do is make sure you stay in office."
Monica wrapped her arms around me.
"You let me worry about that."
entradas.menu: "You let me worry about that."

entradas.text: Monica smiled, took my hand and wordlessly led me upstairs to the bedroom.
"I'm not going to stop until we get what we're asking for. True equality for all women in Sordland."
"With you by my side, how can I lose?"
entradas.menu: "With you by my side, how can I lose?"

entradas.text: "And that's where the real politics begins."
entradas.menu: "And that's where the real politics begins."

entradas.text: "Oh, I always had an idea."
We stayed curled up on the couch till late, talking and reminiscing about old times, until Monica took my hand and wordlessly led me upstairs to the bedroom.
We stayed curled up on the couch, talking about my re-election strategy and the next steps with the women's rights bill, until Monica took my hand and wordlessly led me upstairs to the bedroom.
"Why didn't you talk to me first? Haven't you learned anything this entire time?"
"I didn't get the chance. I'm sorry."
entradas.menu: "I didn't get the chance. I'm sorry."

entradas.text: "You were lucky I let you get involved at all."
entradas.menu: "You were lucky I let you get involved at all."

entradas.text: Monica's eyes flashed.
"Well, we're not going to stop fighting for this. With or without you."
"I know. That's why I married you."
entradas.menu: "I know. That's why I married you."

entradas.text: "Don't you know a lost cause when you see one?"
entradas.menu: "Don't you know a lost cause when you see one?"

entradas.text: Monica scowled and looked straight at me.
"In this case, I do."
Monica smiled wearily.
"I'm not really in the mood to keep talking. It's time for bed."
Without another word, she headed up the stairs, leaving me alone with my thoughts again.
"This would never have happened if you'd supported her."
"This would never have happened if you'd supported us."
"It just wasn't the right time."
entradas.menu: "It just wasn't the right time."

entradas.text: "It was just too risky."
entradas.menu: "It was just too risky."

entradas.text: "You ladies were asking for too much, too quickly."
entradas.menu: "You ladies were asking for too much, too quickly."

entradas.text: "That's bullshit."
"Papa, don't hurt her again! Please!"
All things must come to an end.
All things must come to an end.

It had been a while since Petr disappeared from our lives. I still found myself thinking of jokes he'd find funny or wanting to tell him what had happened at my last meeting. But the grief was beginning to fade.

Monica visited Evelyn often at first, helping her process her mixed emotions. Eventually, Evelyn sold Petr's villa in Erlory and used the proceeds to travel the world, something she'd always wanted to do when she and Petr were together.
For myself and Monica, though, life in the capitol had to go on. And it did.
"I couldn't care less about your women's rights."
entradas.menu: "I couldn't care less about your women's rights."

entradas.text: "So what do you care about?"
entradas.menu: "So what do you care about?"

entradas.text: I leaned in to kiss her, but she pushed me away. I smelled gin on her breath.
entradas.menu: Kiss her.

entradas.text: Monica scowled.
"Come on, Monica. I didn't even care about women's rights until I met you. You're the reason for all of this."
"Come on, Monica. You know I've always cared about this. I wouldn't leave you out of it unless there was a good reason."
"Then why sideline me? I don't understand."
"You had every opportunity to include me. I don't understand."
"What did you expect, Monica? You knew what kind of person I was when you married me."
"I-- I guess I always hoped you would change your mind. But you're right. I was an idiot."
"I'm disappointed too. You must know I tried my best."
"How would I know? I wasn't there."
"I can. I do. I hereby forbid you from divorcing me."
"You will not divorce me, Monica. I forbid it."
Monica gaped at me disbelievingly.
"How can you even say that to me?"
"Who the hell are you, Anton Rayne?"
"I'm the same man I've always been. You just didn't want to see it because you were too focused on your own ambitions."
"I'm a man whose enemies have a habit of... disappearing."
"You're right. This isn't me. Let's just talk for a second."
"Go on, then. It's been over between us for a long time."
She looked at me sadly.
"It has, hasn't it?"
"Ever since that day you hit me on the balcony."
"Ever since you decided to put your political ambitions over your family's happiness."
"Ever since you decided your own political career was worth more than your wife's happiness."
"So it was all my fault?"
"Can we finalize everything after the election, though? A divorce could lose me major points."
Monica gave me a disgusted look.
"It was more complicated than that."
"I wish I could take it back. All of it."
"I know. But in the end, the outcome is the same."
"Say, what about one last romp in the hay? For old times' sake."
"It's a little late."
"So who's getting custody of Deana?"
I reached into my briefcase and pulled out the old photo of the two of us.
entradas.menu: Show her the photograph you took from your old office.

entradas.text: Monica looked at it. Tears began to form in her eyes.
"I hope you can find someone else who makes you as happy as you look here."
"Damn. We used to be hot stuff."
Monica shook her head.
"I-- I'm taking Deana to a hotel tonight. I think it's for the best that we don't see each other for a while."
With one last regretful look at me, Monica trudged upstairs to get Deana.
"Keep it. To remember me."
Monica laughed ruefully.
"Oh, I'll never forget you, Anton. For better or worse."
"Now you're interested in being a good father? For heaven's sake, Anton."
Monica laughed ruefully.
"Look at what politics did to us."
Monica gave me a rueful look.
"Love wasn't the reason I looked so happy back then. It was hope."
"No. God, no! It's too late."
"Maybe everyone else lets you talk to them this way. But I will not."
"I'm the most powerful man in Sordland. Disobey me at your own risk."
She swallowed.
She swallowed.
"That kind of intimidation might work on your political opponents. But not me."
"No, you've changed. You let your power get to your head. Just like Soll."
"You might be right. But it's all crystal clear now."
